result.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
result.summary: Large language models are increasingly used to translate natural language questions about structured data into executable programs. A fundamental challenge is recognizing when a question admits multiple computational interpretations and identifying the decisions needed to resolve them. We investigate whether language models recognize these unresolved decisions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions that may lead to incorrect results. We refer to the latter behavior as Underspecified Decision Completion (UDC). To distinguish different causes of UDC, we introduce Grounded Code Generation (GCG), a diagnostic protocol that separates the identification of unresolved decisions, their resolution using evidence, and their translation into executable code. By examining each stage separately, we can determine where the decisions responsible for incorrect results were first missed or mishandled. We evaluate this framework on BIRD-Pandas with twelve models. The results show that answering clarification questions consistently improves execution accuracy, yet substantial errors remain. Our findings suggest that the main difficulty lies not in answering clarification questions, but in recognizing which questions need to be asked in the first place.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究自然语言查询结构化数据时模型是否在生成代码前识别出未决的多解决策，提出 Grounded Code Generation 诊断协议，把「识别未决决策—用证据解决—转写为可执行代码」分阶段拆开，并在 BIRD-Pandas 上评测十二个模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心发现「难点在于识别该问什么问题而非回答澄清问题」可能为 LVR 中何时继续 LOOK、何时停止并索取视觉证据的问题表述与分阶段评价提供启发，但该工作不涉及视觉状态分析，仅供核查概念迁移。
